# AIVIA platform onboarding

<!-- Generated by `aivia publish docs`; do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Regenerate: aivia publish docs --output docs/PLATFORMS.md -->

This guide walks a new publisher through the six things that must be true before content reaches a platform: the apps you can publish to, the scopes each account needs, the account types AIVIA supports, the audit trail every publish leaves, the quota request checked before a post is sent, and the environment variables that hold credentials. Platform limits are read from the packaged ``platforms.yaml`` data file, so this document stays in sync with the rules code enforces. No provider or network call is made while generating it.

## Apps

AIVIA publishes to the apps below. Each app declares the media types it accepts and the limits every output must meet before it can be posted. Limits come from ``platforms.yaml`` and are enforced by output validation, not by convention.

| App | Name | Media types | Duration | Resolution | Max file | Caption | Hashtags | Disclosure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `instagram` | Instagram Reels | `video`, `image`, `carousel` | 3s min - 900s max | `1080x1920` (9:16) | 1 GB | 2200 | 30 | yes |
| `telegram` | Telegram channel | `video`, `image`, `audio`, `web_card` | 1s min - 3600s max | `1920x1080` (16:9), `1080x1920` (9:16) | 2 GB | 1024 | 20 | no |
| `tiktok` | TikTok | `video` | 3s min - 600s max | `1080x1920` (9:16) | 4 GB | 2200 | 20 | yes |
| `x` | X | `video`, `image` | 1s min - 140s max | `1280x720` (16:9), `720x1280` (9:16), `1080x1080` (1:1) | 512 MB | 280 | 10 | yes |
| `youtube` | YouTube Shorts | `video` | 1s min - 180s max | `1080x1920` (9:16) | 250 GB | 5000 | 15 | yes |

## Scopes

A scope is the permission an account holds on a platform -- for example the right to post, upload media or read insights. AIVIA only publishes through a provider that declares the ``publish`` capability for the target app, and ``aivia publish check`` verifies that scope before any request is sent. An account without the required scope cannot publish, and attempting to do so fails fast with a clear message instead of a silent drop.

## Account types

An account is identified by ``platform/language`` -- for example ``youtube/en`` or ``tiktok/de`` -- and is bound to exactly one platform and one language. An account can be a personal profile or a business page; AIVIA does not distinguish between them in config, so the account type is whatever the connected credential represents. Each account lists the credential references it resolves to (for example an OAuth token or an API key). An account can be disabled without deleting it, which stops publishing to it while keeping its history.

## Audits

Every publish is recorded in an append-only audit trail keyed by an idempotency key. The trail stores the platform, account, profile, language, format, caption, media, visibility, remote identifier and the platform-assigned URL, plus whether the post is a dry run. A repeat attempt with the same idempotency key returns the stored result instead of posting again, so a retry after a timeout can never double post. Only retryable failures are retried; permanent errors such as an auth or invalid request error are surfaced immediately. A publish attestation records who confirmed rights and disclosure, when, the applied disclosure text and the license summary, and strict mode blocks publishing when anything is missing.

## Quota requests

Before a publish is sent, ``aivia publish check`` runs a quota request against the configured budget: the estimated cost is checked against the remaining day, month and per-provider limits and the request is rejected when it would exceed a cap. Budget checks reserve the estimate atomically so concurrent calls cannot both pass the same cap, and on exceeding a limit the run can be downgraded to a cheaper provider, paused as paused budget, or notify only. Quota state is persisted so a restart does not repeat an alert within the same period.

## Environment variables

Credentials live in environment variables, never in config files. A secret reference such as ``OPENAI_API_KEY`` is resolved as ``AIVA_OPENAI_API_KEY`` from the environment, then from the ``secrets.env`` file beside the config, then from the OS keyring. The lookup order is environment, secrets file, keyring. Values are never included in errors or log messages, and resolved config, run snapshots and sidecars are masked so secrets never leak to disk. The ``TOKEN_STORE_KEY`` reference (``AIVA_TOKEN_STORE_KEY``) encrypts stored publish tokens and must be set before publishing.
